subject: Benchmarking acceptance plan for Citrona onboarding
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@citrona.com>, sam.lee@citrona.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Benchmarking acceptance plan for Citrona onboarding

Hi Alex / Sam —

Welcome again — excited to get Citrona live on Redwood. Attached is a concise benchmarking playbook (benchmark-plan-v1.pdf) that lays out the acceptance criteria and a suggested 5-day test cadence we find works well during handoff. High-level asks:

- Confirm the peak traffic shape you expect during the first 30 days (peak RPS, burst patterns, typical request size). Your note in discovery was ~350 rps peak, please confirm.
- Agree the acceptance SLOs below so we can lock the run window:
  - Throughput: sustain 300 rps for 30 minutes with <=5% error rate
  - Latency: p95 < 200 ms, p99 < 450 ms (end-to-end token latency for generation paths), tail-dependent for long prompts
  - Concurrency: support 100 concurrent in-flight sessions with KV cache enabled

Proposed kickoff: Tuesday 2026-11-17 09:00 PT for a short sync (30m) to finalize the run window and ownership. After that, CS + Infra run the load tests, we collect artifacts and share a results bundle for your sign-off.

Artifacts attached / linked: benchmark-plan-v1.pdf, shared drive folder (Drive link below). We typically run Locust-based scenarios and a short smoke run on preprod before the full acceptance exercise.

If that all looks good I’ll hand the run coordination to Monica (cc’d) who will own scheduling and evidence collection.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@citrona.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: sam.lee@citrona.com
Date: 2026-11-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance plan for Citrona onboarding

Thanks Naomi — this is very clear and I appreciate the concise plan. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed peak: 350 rps sustained during business-hour bursts, up to 500 rps for short bursts (<=5 minutes). Most requests are small-ish prompts ~250 tokens on average with occasional long contexts.
- Acceptance targets: your proposed latency bounds look reasonable; we’d prefer p95 < 180 ms if achievable but can accept 200 ms as the primary gate.
- We are OK with the Nov 17 quick sync. Ops (ops@citrona.com) will join and provide test identities and a small whitelist for preprod.

We’ll attach our sample payloads and a small traffic emulator back to you before the sync.

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Product, Citrona

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@citrona.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance plan for Citrona onboarding

Alex — great to have the burst numbers. A couple of concrete items so the acceptance window is unambiguous:

1) Acceptance criteria (final draft):
   - Sustained throughput: 300 rps for 30 minutes (allowed 1 short burst at 500 rps for up to 5m).
   - Errors: <= 5% of requests returning non-200 for the test payloads.
   - Latency: p50, p95, p99 measured at the application boundary. Target p50 < 50 ms, p95 < 200 ms (stretch 180 ms), p99 < 600 ms.
   - Stability: no memory growth or KV cache degradation across a 4-hour soak if we run the extended soak.

2) Test ownership: CS (Monica) will schedule and be primary owner of evidence capture; Infra (Marcus) will configure the load agents and model variants.

3) Model/config: Default: redwood-open-7b (q4) for initial pass; if quantization artifacts appear we’ll try redwood-open-7b-int8 as fallback. Please confirm any custom prompts that change tokenization.

4) Evidence: we will provide a results bundle (results-template.csv) and a directory of raw telemetry (per-request latencies, GPU utilization, kernel metrics). Please upload any customer-side logs to the shared Drive folder.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CitronaOnboardBench
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-8741

I’ve attached the lightweight results template for your review (results-template.csv).

-ben
Ben Carter
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: alex.moreno@citrona.com, ops@citrona.com
Date: 2026-11-16T10:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance plan for Citrona onboarding

Looping in some infra notes and the runbook we’ll use. I’ve included a small Locust scenario pack (locust-scenarios.zip) and a checklist below. Quote of Naomi’s original for context: 

> Proposed kickoff: Tuesday 2026-11-17 09:00 PT for a short sync (30m) to finalize the run window and ownership.

Runbook highlights:
- Precheck (30m before): verify test keys, whitelist IPs, confirm preprod model pinned to redwood-open-7b-q4.
- Smoke (15m): 50 rps ramp to validate correctness and prompt decoding.
- Ramp (45m): linear ramp to 300 rps, hold 30m. Include one 5m spike to 500 rps.
- Soak (optional, 4h): run at steady 150 rps to validate long-term stability. Run only if Citrona signs off on extended testing.
- Metrics to capture: per-request latency (client/server), GPU utilization (per-GPU %), mem footprint, kernel selection logs, KV cache hit ratio, error class breakdown.
- Failure modes & fallback: if p95 > 600 ms during ramp at 300 rps we’ll immediately drop to a compatibility variant and cap concurrency; document rollback time and take snapshot of traces.

File attachments: locust-scenarios.zip (contains locustfile.py + sample payloads) and results-template.csv. I’ll provision a short-lived shared S3 path for raw telemetry after the run.

Marcus Lin
Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: alex.moreno@citrona.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-17T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Benchmarking acceptance plan for Citrona onboarding

Thanks team — this is ready to move to execution. Monica — can you own the scheduling and run-day coordination with Citrona ops? Suggested checklist for the handoff meeting (Nov 17, 09:00 PT):

- 5m introductions / roles (CS = Monica primary, Infra = Marcus primary)
- 10m confirm payloads and whitelist IPs (Citrona ops)
- 10m confirm test shape and acceptance gates (Ben to recap)
- 5m confirm artifact locations and sign-off process (Drive + results-template.csv)

After the run: CS will collect the results bundle, we’ll review within 24 hours and aim to close acceptance within 3 business days provided the artifacts meet the gate. If we miss a gate, Marcus will propose targeted mitigations (batching tweaks, kernel rollback, quantization switch).

Monica — please confirm you’ve got the handoff and add the meeting to Citrona’s calendar. Alex / Sam — if you can send the sample payloads to ops@redwood.com before the meeting that will speed the smoke test.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
